metadata.name: peard_vault
metadata.description: PEARD ASSETS: the reserve of real things behind a token, and what each one is worth today

docs: The reserve of real things behind a token.
Three programs now, and each owns exactly one question. peard owns
what a token is counted in. peard_amm owns where it trades. This owns
what is actually in the room, and what that is worth today.
It holds NFTs. An NFT here is a deed to a specific batch of a specific
thing, and making it an instance rather than a registry row is the point:
pears bought in September and pears bought in March share a name and
nothing else. Every variable that decides value - shrink, expiry, carry,
haircut, who is holding it, what was paid - is a field on the batch.
The core values nothing itself. It stores an appraisal, applies the same
oracle discipline peard uses on prices, and subtracts what holding the
thing has cost. How a pear lot or a graded card gets its number is an
appraiser's problem, and appraisers are per item.

instructions.name: attach_receipt_mint
docs: Name the fungible receipt for this reserve. Once, and never again.
The reserve PDA must already be the mint authority and the supply must
be zero, both checked here rather than trusted. A mint somebody else
can issue is not a receipt for anything: it is a claim on this room
that this room did not make.
One-way for the same reason `asset_mint` is immutable in the registry.
Repointing would leave outstanding receipts claiming a room that no
longer acknowledges them, and there is no honest thing to do with
those afterwards.

accounts.name: receipt_mint
docs: Checked by hand: the reserve must already be its authority, the supply
must be zero, and it must carry no freeze authority.

instructions.name: burn_receipts
docs: Hand receipts back and stop claiming that many items.
Permissionless: burning is giving something up, and nobody needs
permission to do that. It exists as its own instruction because a
redemption is not the only reason to want out, and because the
invariant has to be restorable before `items_held` falls.

instructions.name: close_epoch
docs: Close the epoch once every held item has been marked.
All or nothing on purpose. A partially marked reserve is worse than
an unmarked one, because it looks current: the items somebody
bothered to crank are the ones that went up.

instructions.name: deposit_item
docs: Take custody of a deed and record everything about the batch.
The opening appraisal is the cost basis, which is the only figure
nobody has to be trusted about: it is what was actually paid. Every
later number is somebody's opinion, and the breaker is what stops an
opinion moving too far in one step.

instructions.name: issue_receipts
docs: Issue receipts against items actually held.
`items` is whole items, and the cap is the invariant stated plainly:
receipts outstanding may never exceed what is in the room. Nothing
here consults an appraisal, deliberately. Value moves with the market
and the count does not, and a receipt is a claim on a THING rather
than on a number: pegging issuance to value would let a rising mark
mint claims that no crate stands behind.

instructions.name: mark_item
docs: Bring one item's contribution to the aggregate up to date.
Permissionless, because everything it can do is lower a number that
otherwise sits high: carry accrues, expiry arrives, an appraisal goes
stale. Nobody has an incentive to crank a reserve they are long, so
the freshness gate below is what makes it happen rather than goodwill.

accounts.name: reserve
docs: SEEDED ON THE AUTHORITY AS WELL AS THE MARKET, and this is a fix.
`market` is an instruction ARGUMENT, not an account: nothing checks
the caller's relationship to it. On the old seeds a stranger could
claim the canonical reserve and backing for any market in the
registry, name themselves custodian, and keep them: peard_vault has no
admin, no `close_reserve` and no authority transfer, so the claim was
permanent and free.
Seeding on the authority makes a squat self-inflicted. It costs the
property that a reader could derive the address from the market
alone, which was never load-bearing: peard_perps reaches a backing
through the address pinned on its own market by `set_backing`, and
peard_amm through `pool.backing_reserve`. Both are stored, and both
are checked against the reserve's own contents rather than against a
derivation.

instructions.name: push_appraisal
docs: What the thing is worth now, according to whoever is allowed to say.
The discipline is lifted wholesale from peard's oracle, because it
is the same problem wearing different clothes: a step past the
breaker freezes the item rather than moving it, and a frozen item
refuses pushes so the figure cannot be walked while nobody is
counting it.

instructions.name: redeem_item
docs: Hand the deed over. Somebody is taking the actual thing.
The join to peard is a transaction, not a call. There, a holder
burns units and the request is settled; here, the deed leaves the
reserve. Bundling both in one transaction makes it atomic without
either program having to know the other exists, which is the same
seam the fee route already uses.
Redeemed is not written off. The thing left because it was delivered,
and a reserve that cannot tell those two apart cannot tell you
whether its custodian is good for anything.

instructions.name: roll_position
docs: Unfreeze an item somebody has looked at.
Roll a dated position into the next one, in a single instruction.
This is how a perpetual claim is built out of contracts that expire.
A futures contract tracks its underlying because delivery forces
convergence, and the price of that anchor is an expiry date. Holding
exposure past it means selling the expiring month and buying the next,
forever, which is what a commodity ETF does and what `successor` on a
pairable has always been for.
ATOMIC, and not by preference. `receipts_issued <= items_held` is the
invariant that makes a receipt mean anything, and a roll done as a
write-off followed by a deposit would drop `items_held` below the
receipts in between and be refused. One instruction, one swap, and the
count never dips. Receipts are untouched throughout: that is the whole
point of the exercise, since the claim is perpetual and only the thing
underneath it has a date on it.
The roll economics are recorded in USD rather than inferred. `proceeds`
is what closing the expiring position realised and `cost` is what the
replacement took, both quoted in the reserve's own dollar. When the
next month is dearer the difference is a loss that recurs every roll
and compounds, and a holder who cannot see it accumulating is the USO
holder of 2020: right about oil, eaten by the roll.

accounts.name: successor
docs: against `old_item.rolls_into` and against the registry pinned on the
reserve, then parsed for its expiry and its own successor.

instructions.name: settle_carry
docs: Pay the custodian what storing the thing has actually cost.
Permissionless to crank and destination-fixed: it can only ever pay
the address recorded on the item. Carry is a claim ahead of holders,
so it sits as a debt against the item's value until it is settled;
settling it lifts the value back by the amount paid, which is correct
rather than generous, because somebody put money in to clear it.
An empty carry vault is not an error worth aborting a crank over. It
is the operator behind on the warehouse bill, and the debt staying
visible on the item is the honest outcome.

instructions.name: write_off_item
docs: It is gone and it was not delivered.
A pallet dropped, a crop failed, a card never arrived. Recorded as a
loss against the custodian rather than quietly netted off the value,
because the difference between "worth less" and "missing" is the
whole question of whether the custodian is good for it.

types.name: AppraisalRejected
docs: The breaker tripped. Worth an event of its own: an appraiser trying to
move a figure further than the reserve allows is a fact about the
appraiser, not just about the item.

types.name: Backing
docs: What this reserve is worth, published for anyone to read.
Deliberately tiny and deliberately frozen. It exists so that a program
which should not depend on this one can still price the backing: it
derives the address from the market, checks the owner and the magic, and
reads six numbers. Nothing here is a pointer into peard_vault's internals,
so peard_vault can be rewritten without breaking a reader.
`as_of_ts` is the moment an epoch last closed with EVERY item marked. A
reader that ignores it is reading a number that only ever drifts upward
of the truth.

fields.name: value_usd
docs: Net of haircut and unpaid carry, USD e6.

types.name: Item
docs: One deed, and every variable that decides what it is worth today.

fields.name: nft_mint
docs: The NFT that stands for this batch. The reserve holds it.

fields.name: appraiser
docs: Who may appraise it. Per item, because a card grader and a produce
inspector are not the same party and should not share a key.

fields.name: custodian
docs: Who physically has the thing and owes delivery on it.

fields.name: quantity
docs: Units of the underlying: cartons, ounces, hours, one card.

fields.name: cost_basis_usd
docs: Total paid, USD e6.

fields.name: rolls_into
docs: The contract this position rolls into, or default for none.
THE ROLL TERM, carried by the position itself rather than decided by
whoever happens to be holding the keys when the month turns. A dated
contract that names its successor cannot be rolled anywhere else: the
program checks the replacement against this address and against that
pairable's own expiry, so "it rolls into the next month" stops being a
promise and becomes a thing the chain enforces.
Set at deposit and inherited on every roll from the successor's OWN
successor, so the strip walks itself forward without anybody
re-declaring it.

fields.name: expires_ts
docs: 0 means it does not expire. Past this the item is worth nothing, and
that is a cliff rather than a taper on purpose: a pear in controlled
atmosphere is fine for months and then it is not.

fields.name: carry_bps_per_day
docs: Storage, insurance and custody, bps of appraised value per day. The
negative yield on holding real things, and the variable most likely
to be forgotten until it has quietly eaten the backing.

fields.name: haircut_bps
docs: Taken off every appraisal, bps. A pear lot is not USDC, and a basket
that marks it as though it were will overstate coverage by exactly
the amount that matters in the moment it matters.

fields.name: appraised_usd
docs: Latest appraisal for the whole item, USD e6, before haircut or carry.

fields.name: last_step_bps
docs: How far the last accepted appraisal moved, bps. A receipt.

fields.name: frozen
docs: Refuses appraisals as well as counting. Freezing and still accepting
pushes would let the value be walked to anywhere during the freeze.

fields.name: carry_owed_usd
docs: Carry run up and not yet paid, USD e6.
Subtracted from the item's value because it is a real claim ahead of
holders: the warehouse is owed it whether or not anybody has paid. It
falls when the custodian is settled, and the value rises to meet it,
which is correct - somebody put money in.

fields.name: marked_value_usd
docs: Contribution to `Reserve.value_usd` as of the last mark.

types.name: ItemKind
docs: What an item is.
Metadata, never dispatch. Nothing in this program branches on it, and
that is the whole design: "we need to support every type" is only
tractable if the core supports none of them specifically. A kind decides
which appraiser is credible and what a haircut means, and both of those
live outside.

fields.name: drag_usd
docs: Positive is the drag: what this roll cost over what it returned.

fields.name: quantity_before
docs: The other half of the same fact, and the half a holder feels.
Cash drag and quantity shrinkage are two ways of paying for the same
roll: top up to keep the tonnage, or take the proceeds and hold less.
Reporting only the first lets the second happen silently.

fields.name: cumulative_drag_usd
docs: And what every roll has cost, so the compounding is legible without
replaying the log.

types.name: Reserve
docs: The reserve of real things behind one market.
It holds NFTs and nothing else. Each NFT is the deed to a specific batch
of a specific thing, and the reason to make it an NFT rather than a row
is that the variables live on the batch: pears bought in September and
pears bought in March are not the same asset, and no registry entry can
be true of both.

fields.name: market
docs: The market this backs. Never read here. Provenance, and the reason a
reserve means anything at all.

fields.name: value_usd
docs: Sum of every held item's net value as of its last mark, USD e6.
Only meaningful together with `epoch_closed_ts`. Carry and expiry
only ever push a value down, so a reserve nobody has marked is a
reserve overstating itself, which is why staleness disqualifies the
whole number rather than one item.

fields.name: cost_basis_usd
docs: What was actually paid for everything still held, USD e6. Solvency
against cost is a different question from solvency against the mark,
and both are worth being able to ask.

fields.name: carry_accrued_usd
docs: Storage, insurance and custody charged so far, USD e6. A real
warehouse bleeds even when nothing spoils.

fields.name: carry_paid_usd
docs: And how much of it the custodian has actually been handed.

fields.name: usd_mint
docs: The mint carry is settled in. Pinned, for the same reason peard
pins its dollar: "USDC" is a symbol anyone can mint.

fields.name: epoch
docs: Marking runs in epochs so freshness is one comparison rather than a
scan over every item.

fields.name: epoch_closed_ts
docs: When the last epoch closed with every item marked. Zero until one has.

fields.name: max_mark_age_secs
docs: Past this, the aggregate is refused rather than believed.

fields.name: breaker_bps
docs: Ceiling on a single appraisal step, bps. Trips into a freeze.

fields.name: receipt_mint
docs: The fungible receipt for what is in the room, or default for none.
This is what makes a warehouse tradeable. Items are individual and a
crate is not interchangeable with a crate in another row, but a
STANDARDISED item is: that is the whole reason an exchange writes a
grade into the contract. One receipt is one held item at that grade,
so receipts are fungible where the items only nearly are, and a
fungible thing is the only thing an AMM can hold.
The reserve PDA is the mint authority. Nobody else can issue.

fields.name: registry_program
docs: The program whose contract specifications this warehouse honours.
Pinned at opening and never changed, for the same reason peard_perps pins
its registry: a warehouse that could be pointed at a different notion
of "next month" is a warehouse whose roll terms mean nothing.

fields.name: soonest_expiry_ts
docs: The soonest any held item expires, or 0 when nothing does.
THE CLOCK. Without it a receipt whose item expires in a week looks
exactly like one whose item expires in a year, and the difference is
the entire risk a holder is carrying. Maintained on deposit and on
roll rather than scanned, because a program cannot walk its own items
cheaply and a number nobody can afford to read is not a warning.
It is a floor rather than an exact minimum: a roll can only ever push
it later, so after several rolls it may name a date earlier than any
item actually has. That errs toward warning too early, which is the
direction to be wrong in.

fields.name: roll_cost_usd
docs: What rolling has cost, USD e6, and what it has returned. Monotonic.
THE NUMBER THAT KILLED USO. A perpetual claim built out of dated
contracts has to roll: sell the expiring month, buy the next. When the
next month is dearer the difference is a real loss, paid every roll,
and it compounds. USO's holders in 2020 were not wrong about oil, they
were eaten by the roll, and the reason they did not see it coming is
that nothing reported it.
Two counters rather than one signed net, so a reserve cannot quietly
offset a run of losses against one good roll. The drag is
`roll_cost_usd - roll_proceeds_usd` and a holder is entitled to both
halves.

fields.name: rolls
docs: How many times. A drag of the same size over two rolls and over fifty
are different facts about a position.

fields.name: receipts_issued
docs: Receipts outstanding, counted in WHOLE ITEMS rather than base units.
The invariant is `receipts_issued <= items_held`, and it is the whole
point: a receipt that outnumbers the thing it claims is a promise the
room cannot keep. Comparing in items rather than in base units keeps
the check independent of the mint's decimals, which are a display
choice and should not be able to move a solvency test.
